Check the feasibility of a grafting plan before grafting

Source: R/check_grafting_plan.R
check_grafting_plan.Rd

Check, before any grafting, whether the taxa (or missing clades) of missing_taxa_list can be grafted** on the backbone phy with the constraints chosen (target clades, excluded subclades, stem availability, species attributes), and report what is available for each of them: the number of branches, the share of the available branches that is in the allowed states (if simmap is used as a constraint), the time window of the divergence ages and the share of it where grafting is possible, and the allowed states found along the valid branches.

The goal is to help fine-tune the grafting constraints before committing to a long run: the same checks are run at the start of phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() and phylograftR::graft_missing_clades() (which stop if a taxon cannot be grafted), but here the problems are reported for all the taxa at once, and the table can be explored.

Usage

check_grafting_plan(
  phy,
  missing_taxa_list,
  min_tips = 5,
  include_target_clade_stem = TRUE,
  use_excluded_subclades = TRUE,
  exclude_subclades_stem = TRUE,
  simmap = NULL,
  allowed_states = NULL,
  treat_states_as_ranges = FALSE,
  min_valid_fraction = 0.1,
  ultrametric_tol = .Machine$double.eps^0.5,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

phy

An object of class "phylo". The backbone phylogeny: time-calibrated (ultrametric) and binary.

missing_taxa_list

A list, as given to the grafting functions (see phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() and phylograftR::graft_missing_clades()). Items: $Taxon_name, and $Target_clade (taxa, for graft_missing_taxa()) or $Sister_clade (missing clades, for graft_missing_clades()), with the optional items of the grafting function. Exactly one of $Target_clade and $Sister_clade must be provided: it defines the type of the plan.

It can also be the list of both types of lineages to graft, list(taxa = ..., clades = ...), as returned by phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list() when both types are provided, to be used with phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa_and_clades(). Each part is then planned on the same backbone and the output is a named list (see 'Value').

min_tips

Numeric. Same as in the grafting functions. With method = "BD_clades", a birth-death model is fitted on the target clade (or the sister clade) of each taxon, or on the smallest enclosing clade with at least min_tips tips. Here, no model is fitted: the enclosing clade is only reported. Default is 5.

include_target_clade_stem, use_excluded_subclades, exclude_subclades_stem

Same as in phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa(). Only used with a $Target_clade list.

simmap

NULL, or stochastic character map(s) of the backbone, as in the grafting functions (a "simmap", a "multiSimmap", or a list of them for several traits). Used to constrain grafting based on the matching of the allowed_states of each taxa with the states found along branches of the stochastic character map(s).

allowed_states, treat_states_as_ranges

Same as in the grafting functions. Only used with a simmap.

min_valid_fraction

Numeric between 0 and 1. Taxa (or missing clades) with a share of available branches in allowed states below this value are flagged as low_valid_fraction (a warning in the grafting functions). Default is 0.1.

ultrametric_tol

Numeric. Tolerance used by ape::is.ultrametric() to check for ultrametricity. Default is .Machine$double.eps^0.5.

verbose

Logical. Print a summary? Default is TRUE.

Value

A data.frame with one row per taxon ($Target_clade list) or per missing clade ($Sister_clade list). With a list(taxa, clades) covering both types of missing lineages, the output is a named list with the elements taxa and clades, each data.frame containing the output of its type (as described below), and the overarching attribute "all_feasible" (TRUE if all the missing taxa and missing clades can be grafted).

Columns for missing taxa:

  • Taxon_name Character string. Name of the taxon.

  • Target_clade Character string. Tips defining the target clade (first five).

  • target_n_tips Integer. Number of tips of the target clade in the backbone.

  • n_branches Integer. Number of branches available for grafting (before the restriction to the allowed states).

  • window_age Numeric. Upper end (age) of the time window of the divergence ages: the stem age of the target clade, or its crown age if the stem is not available for grafting.

  • enclosing_n_tips, enclosing_age Integer and numeric. Number of tips in the backbone phylogeny, and crown age of the enclosing clade (see Details).

Columns for missing clades:

  • Missing_clade Integer. ID of the missing clade (taxa with the same sister clade).

  • Taxa Character string. Taxa of the missing clade, separated by commas.

  • Sister_clade Character string. Tips defining the sister clade (first five).

  • sister_n_tips Integer. Number of tips of the sister clade in the backbone.

  • stem_length Numeric. Length of the stem branch of the sister clade.

  • stem_age Numeric. Age of the rootward end of the stem branch: the upper end of the divergence ages.

  • enclosing_n_tips, enclosing_age Integer and numeric. Number of tips in the backbone phylogeny, and crown age of the enclosing clade (see Details).

Columns for any type, with a simmap:

  • allowed_states Character string. The allowed states (resolved among the states of the simmap).

  • states_available Character string. The states found in the available branches.

  • valid_fraction, time_coverage Numeric. Share of the length of the available branches in allowed states, and share of the time window where at least one available branch is in an allowed state. With several maps: valid_fraction_min, valid_fraction_mean, valid_fraction_max, and the same for time_coverage.

  • n_maps_infeasible Integer. With several maps, the number of maps where the taxon (or missing clade) cannot be grafted.

Last columns:

  • feasible Logical. Can the taxon be grafted (in all the maps)?

  • cause Character string. Why it cannot be grafted:

    • "excluded": no branch left by the constraints;

    • "excluded_contains_target": an excluded subclade contains the target clade;

    • "excluded_identical": an excluded subclade is identical to the target clade;

    • "allowed_states": no available branch has a piece in an allowed state;

    • "whole_tree": the sister clade is the whoel tree, thus no stem branch exists for grafting;

    • "inconsistent_allowed_states": the taxa of a missing clade have different allowed states;

    • "low_valid_fraction": the share of available branche pieces in allowed states is below min_valid_fraction;

    • "none": no issue. With several maps, the causes found across all maps are concatenated, separated by "|".

Attributes: "type" ("taxa" or "clades"), "min_tips", "min_valid_fraction", "n_maps", and "per_map" (with several maps: the diagnostic table of each map, with a map column).

Details

Taxa ($Target_clade list)

For each taxon, the pool of branches available for grafting is built from its target clade, and restricted by its excluded subclades (see phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa()). With a simmap, the pool is then restricted to the pieces of the branches in the allowed states of the taxon.

Missing clades ($Sister_clade list)

Taxa with the same sister clade are grafted together as one missing clade. The missing clade is grafted on the stem branch of its sister clade (see phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa()). With a simmap the share of the stem branch in the allowed states is both the valid fraction and the share of the time window available. The taxa of a missing clade must share their allowed states. Results of the evaluation are reported with one row per missing clade.

Enclosing clade

The enclosing clade is the target clade (or sister clade), or the smallest clade enclosing it with at least min_tips tips, in the backbone. With method = "BD_clades", it is used to fit the Birth-Death model and estimate divergence ages of the missing taxa to graft in accordance to the fitted diversification process. It is reported so users can tune min_tips accordingly to define more relevant enclosing clades. During the grafting, taxa already grafted in a clade count in its number of tips. The chosen enclosing clade used can therefore be the reported clade or a clade nested within it. It can contain more tips than the one reported here, although the reported clade is the oldest one that can be used, and the number of tips reported is its number of backbone tips.

The sampling fractions of the birth-death models are not reported: they depend on the taxa already grafted in the clade, so they cannot be known before grafting. Use phylograftR::extract_BD_model_summary() to extract a posteriori the effective sampling fraction and diversification rates used during the grafting process.

Several maps

With a "multiSimmap", the plan is checked for each map, as attribute-based constraints are different across maps, and the table summarizes values across all maps (i.e., minimum, mean and maximum of the valid fraction and of the time coverage, and the number of maps in which the taxon cannot be grafted). The table per map is stored in the attribute "per_map".

See also

Other functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() to graft taxa based on target clades and excluded subclades.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_clades() to graft groups of missing taxa as sister clades of backbone clades.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa_and_clades() to graft missing taxa and missing clades in one run, with a single set of inputs.

  • phylograftR::check_grafting_constraints() to check a posteriori that grafted taxa respect their constraints, after grafting.

  • phylograftR::extract_grafting_info() to extract a posteriori information on the location of grafted lineages.

  • phylograftR::extract_sampling_info() to extract a posteriori the richness and the sampling fraction of the clades in each grafted phylogeny.

  • phylograftR::extract_BD_model_summary() to extract a posteriori information on the birth-death models fitted during grafting.

Author

Maël Doré

Examples

# --- Prepare data --- #

# Create a toy backbone phylogeny and associated list of missing taxa
set.seed(1234)
phy <- ape::rcoal(n = 30)
phy$edge.length <- phy$edge.length / max(ape::node.depth.edgelength(phy)) * 50

missing_taxa_list <- list(
  Taxon_name = c("X1", "X2", "X3"),
  Target_clade = list(X1 = c("t26", "t18"), X2 = c("t8", "t22"), X3 = "t5"))

# --- Check the grafting plan for taxonomic constraints --- #

# Check the grafting plan a priori to detect any issue at low cost
plan <- check_grafting_plan(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list, min_tips = 5)
#> Grafting plan: 3 taxa
#>   - Can be grafted: 3/3
#>   - Target clades smaller than 'min_tips' = 5 (birth-death model fitted on an enclosing clade): 1/3; enclosing clades of 13 tips in the backbone; in practice, the clade used can be nested within them, as previously grafted taxa count towards 'min_tips'
#>   => All can be grafted with these constraints
plan
#>   Taxon_name Target_clade target_n_tips n_branches window_age enclosing_n_tips
#> 1         X1     t26, t18            17         33 50.0000000               17
#> 2         X2      t8, t22            13         25 50.0000000               13
#> 3         X3           t5             1          1  0.6368624               13
#>   enclosing_age feasible cause
#> 1      20.03438     TRUE  none
#> 2      15.28106     TRUE  none
#> 3      15.28106     TRUE  none

# --- Check the grafting plan for attribute-based constraints too --- #

# Add a simmap to restrict grafting to some states
Q <- matrix(0.04, 3, 3, dimnames = list(c("A", "B", "C"), c("A", "B", "C")))
diag(Q) <- -0.08
simmap <- phytools::sim.history(phy, Q, anc = "A", message = FALSE)

# Check the grafting plan a priori
plan_states <- check_grafting_plan(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,
                                   simmap = simmap, allowed_states = "B")
#> Grafting plan: 3 taxa
#>   - Can be grafted: 2/3
#>   - Cannot be grafted (1):
#>       allowed_states              1
#>       e.g., X3
#>   - Share of the available branches in allowed states (feasible taxa): min 8.1%, median 13.4%
#>   - Share of the time window with grafting possible (feasible taxa): min 8.6%, median 19.1%
#>   - Below 'min_valid_fraction' = 0.1 (1): X1
#>   - Target clades smaller than 'min_tips' = 5 (birth-death model fitted on an enclosing clade): 1/3; enclosing clades of 13 tips in the backbone; in practice, the clade used can be nested within them, as previously grafted taxa count towards 'min_tips'
#>   => Some cannot be grafted with these constraints (see the table)
# Inspect availability of branches in the allowed states
plan_states[, c("Taxon_name", "states_available", "valid_fraction", "time_coverage", "feasible")]
#>   Taxon_name states_available valid_fraction time_coverage feasible
#> 1         X1          A, B, C     0.08115666    0.08617336     TRUE
#> 2         X2          A, B, C     0.18601114    0.29636500     TRUE
#> 3         X3                C     0.00000000    0.00000000    FALSE

# --- Check both types of missing lineages at once --- #

# With list(taxa, clades), each part is planned on the same backbone: the output is a named list
both_list <- list(
  taxa = missing_taxa_list,
  clades = list(Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2"), Sister_clade = list(M1 = c("t8", "t22"), M2 = "t5")))
plans <- check_grafting_plan(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = both_list, verbose = FALSE)
names(plans)
#> [1] "taxa"   "clades"
# "all_feasible" is TRUE if both types of missing lineages are feasible
attr(plans, "all_feasible")
#> [1] TRUE
